title: Sydney is on daylight saving time in January and off it in July -- the opposite of New York
assumption: Daylight saving time is 'on' roughly March through November and 'off' in the winter months.

input.display: Australia/Sydney: UTC+11 (DST) in January, UTC+10 (standard) in July; America/New_York: UTC-4 (DST) in July, UTC-5 (standard) in January
input.description: A 'business hours' or 'is it currently DST' heuristic that hardcodes a month range, applied to users in the Southern Hemisphere.

what_goes_wrong: A heuristic like 'DST is active for timestamps between March and November' (true for most of the Northern Hemisphere) silently inverts for Australian, South American, and other Southern Hemisphere users, who are in DST during the Northern Hemisphere's winter.
why: Daylight saving time is tied to each hemisphere's local summer, when the extra evening daylight is wanted, so the Southern Hemisphere's DST season (roughly October to April) runs opposite to the Northern Hemisphere's (roughly March to November). There is no universal 'DST months' rule in the tz database; each zone's transition rule is independent and the only correct way to know whether DST is active at a given instant is to ask the zone, not a hardcoded month range.

repros.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime

sydney = ZoneInfo("Australia/Sydney")
ny = ZoneInfo("America/New_York")
jan_sydney = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=sydney)
jul_sydney = datetime(2024, 7, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=sydney)
jan_ny = datetime(2024, 1, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=ny)
jul_ny = datetime(2024, 7, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=ny)
print("Sydney Jan DST active:", jan_sydney.dst() != __import__('datetime').timedelta(0), "| Jul DST active:", jul_sydney.dst() != __import__('datetime').timedelta(0))
print("New York Jan DST active:", jan_ny.dst() != __import__('datetime').timedelta(0), "| Jul DST active:", jul_ny.dst() != __import__('datetime').timedelta(0))
repros.expected_output:
Sydney Jan DST active: True | Jul DST active: False
New York Jan DST active: False | Jul DST active: True

Sydney Jan offset (min): 660 | Jul offset (min): 600
New York Jan offset (min): -300 | Jul offset (min): -240

fix: Never infer whether DST is active from the calendar month. Ask the timezone library for the UTC offset (or, in Python, the `.dst()` component) at the specific instant and zone you care about.
